entities.text: ORAL ORDER Sri A Thippeswamy vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The lands of the petitioners which are the subject matter of the writ petition were sought to be acquired for the purposes of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board and the preliminary notification was issued on 11.12.2009 and the final notification was issued on 14.06.2010.
However, thereafter no award has been passed and the acquisition proceedings have not been completed.
On the ground that due to unreasonable inordinate delay in passing the award the acquisition proceedings are liable to be quashed, the present writ petition is filed.

2. The aforementioned facts are not disputed by the learned counsel for the respondents and it is admitted that though the final notification was issued in the year 2010, no award has been passed so far.

3. Though specific time is not stipulated under the provisions of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 ('the KIAD Act' for short) for passing the award, NC: 2024:KHC:37093 the acquisition proceedings have to be completed within a reasonable time.
Not passing the award even after nearly 14 years from the date of issuance of the final notification has to be considered unreasonable.
In the acquisition proceedings the land loser will be entitled to compensation as on the date of the preliminary notification.
In the instant case, the preliminary notification is of the year 2009.

Today, if the lands of the petitioners are acquired by the State Authorities and if the petitioners are given compensation as per the value of the lands in the year 2009, it would lead to gross injustice.

As per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, time limit for passing the award has been fixed at two years and as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the time limit for passing the award after issuance of the final notification is fixed at one year extendable by giving reasons.
NC: 2024:KHC:37093 4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Though the said provisions are not applicable when the acquisition is made under the KIAD Act,
the spirit of the said enactments should not be lost sight of while determining as to whether the acquisition proceedings are being completed within a reasonable period or not.

Merely because the KIAD Act does not stipulate the time limit within which an award has to be passed and the lands vest with the Government under Section 28(5) of the KIAD Act upon issuance of the final notification under Section 28(4) of the KIAD Act, it cannot be a ground to justify the inordinate delay in passing the award.
The inordinate delay in passing the award has to be considered unreasonable, unjust and unfair to the petitioners for the reasons mentioned above.
5. For the aforementioned reasons, the writ petition succeeds and the following order is passed:

ORDER (i) The preliminary notification bearing No.CI 530 S.P.Q 2009 dated 11.12.2009 vide Annexure-C NC: 2024:KHC:37093 to the writ petition and the final notification bearing No.CI 339 S.P.Q 2010 dated 14.06.2010 vide Annexure-G to the writ petition are hereby set aside insofar as it relates to the lands of the petitioners, which are the subject matter of the writ petition;
